failure.heading: 16. A session stopped placing its messages once the window said nothing moved — 2026-10-03

observed_failure.description: An independently prompted work turn has no placement call in its public action span before the reply. The hook still gives an unchanged window.

events.text:
The session check holds: an unregistered tag is refused and pointed to `--wake`, and this slice doesn't change that.

**The fourth finding is yours to decide: Q1 never says where the script is or how to run it.**

Every rule says just `questions.py`. Q1 runs every turn, yet nowhere in tier 1 names the path `.agents/scripts/gw/questions.py` or the interpreter. This session paid for that. At the start I ran `python` and got *"Python was not found"*, then had to `find` the script and switch to `py`. Every fresh session pays the same search. Meanwhile the hooks already use the exact form, `uv run --offline --no-project python "<root>/.agents/scripts/gw/questions.py"`, and so does the verification set. Core already depends on `uv`, so recipient trees have it.

- **A. Q1 names the invocation once (recommended).** One clause after the first mention, for example: *"`questions.py` is `.agents/scripts/gw/questions.py`, run with `uv run --offline --no-project python`"*. The examples stay short as `questions.py …`.
  - *For:* it removes a search every session pays, at the cost of about fifteen tier-1 words.
  - *Against:* tier-1 words are paid by every session.
- **B. Leave it bare.** The agent finds the script once per session, as it does today.
  - *For:* no tier-1 words.
  - *Against:* the failure this session hit stays.
- **C. Spell out the full invocation in each example.**
  - *For:* nothing to look up.
  - *Against:* about three times the words of A, for the same information.

Which do you choose?
